resources.string: Translation settings are incomplete: %1$s is missing.
Complete it under Settings → Subtitle translation and try again.
The key may be wrong or expired; some providers bind keys to a region, so using one across regions fails authentication.
Account balance or quota is used up (HTTP %1$d).
Top up in the provider console first; retrying only drains the remaining quota faster.
The provider asks for a %1$d second wait. Just retry afterwards.
Wait a moment and retry; if it keeps happening the provider is congested.
Usually the model name does not exist, or that model does not accept this request shape.
The provider hit an internal error (HTTP %1$d).
Not caused by your settings. Retrying later may help; if it persists, check the provider status page.
The response shape is wrong (this is not a quota problem).
Retrying usually returns the same result. Switch to a more reliable model, or try another provider.
The model produced no output at all this time%1$s.
This usually means reasoning mode used up the entire output budget%1$s. A model without reasoning should translate normally.
This batch is too long and the output was truncated.%1$s
The limit is %1$d tokens, and %2$sthis batch still does not fit after automatic splitting. Use a model with a higher single-response limit.
"is estimated to need about %1$d tokens, so "
Base URL (must start with http:// or https://)
" (request timed out. Long subtitles take a while; raise the read timeout in settings)"
" (the domain could not be resolved: check the address spelling and your network)"
" (plain HTTP was blocked by the system policy; only localhost and 10.0.2.2 are allowed)"

Bailian keys are bound to a region, so using one across regions fails authentication. With a workspace enabled, the address must use the workspace-specific domain, such as https://<WorkspaceId>.cn-beijing.maas.aliyuncs.com/compatible-mode/v1.
Just the domain; the request path is appended for you.
The official docs state that thinking is on by default, so the disable parameter must always be sent; otherwise long subtitles consume a large amount of tokens.
For an Ollama running on this machine, use http://localhost:11434/v1. Plain HTTP on the LAN is blocked by the system policy; only localhost and 10.0.2.2 are allowed.
Any value works for a local service, or leave it empty
Networks in mainland China usually need a proxy; point the address at your own relay service.
Any service with an OpenAI-compatible /chat/completions endpoint works: OpenAI, DeepSeek, Qwen, GLM, Kimi, Ollama, vLLM, LM Studio, one-api relays, and more.
